title: Thresholded Continuum Coalescer: hybrid admission & kernel-aware batch shaping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a 'Thresholded Continuum Coalescer' (TCC) that reduces tail latencies for continuous batching by combining probabilistic admission control, dynamic threshold shaping, and kernel-aware coalescing. TCC targets microbursts and heterogeneous token lengths while preserving throughput and minimizing wasted GPU kernel launches. Key ideas: time-window + capacity threshold hybrid admission, per-tenant soft-reservations, attention-spike detection to pin kernel choices, and a decode handoff protocol to avoid prefill stalls.
acceptance_criteria: P99 prefill+decode latency across synthetic mixed-workload tests improves by >=20% vs current baseline under identical QPS and model mix
No regression in median throughput for steady-state traffic (<5% variance) on benchmark instances
Kernel selection decisions documented and measurable via runtime trace (trace tags: tcc.kernel_hint, tcc.admit_reason)
Rollout can be toggled per-cluster via feature flag and has an automatic rollback if p99 increases by >10% over a 10-minute window
E2E canary run on dedicated pools for two customers with different burst profiles without customer-visible errors
implementation_notes: Admission: implement dual-trigger admission window W and token-capacity threshold C. If either window time elapses or accumulated token-count >= C, emit batch for scheduling.
Probabilistic admission for microbursts: when queue length spikes, probabilistically accept a fraction of new prefill requests to preserve slot headroom and avoid kernel thrash.

Kernel-awareness: annotate queued requests with expected kernel class (int8/cuda/fused-attention hint) from model profile; prefer coalescing requests with same kernel hint within window to reduce kernel switches.

Attention-spike detection: run fast lightweight heuristic on prefill (delta in avg head-attention magnitude across prefixes) to mark 'attention-spike' requests and reserve small 'fast-path' slots to handle them with low-latency kernels.

Decode handoff protocol: when decode request arrives for a stream with prefill partially in-flight, use an in-memory reservation ticket to map decode to the prefetched KV cache to avoid redundant prefill kernel runs.
Per-tenant credit buckets: simple token-bucket credits with refill rates derived from committed capacity to avoid noisy neighbors; credits can be consumed by the probabilistic admission filter.

Telemetry: emit admission_reason, window_elapsed, capacity_triggered, kernel_hint, attention_spike boolean, and reservation_ticket id as traceable fields per request. Add summary metrics for admitted_batch_size, batch_entropy(distribution of sequence lengths), and p99 by kernel_hint.
Safety: keep maximum batching window hard cap (W_max) configurable to prevent unbounded latency under backpressure. Default W_max=30ms for 512-token median workloads.
Config knobs: W_target, C_target, microburst_prob_floor, per_tenant_credit_rate, attention_spike_threshold. Expose via console tuning for Dedicated customers.
Testing: unit tests for admission logic, integration test with kernel scheduler stub, and back-to-back load tests for microburst and steady-state scenarios.
risks: Incorrect kernel_hint tagging could lead to suboptimal coalescing and extra kernel switches, increasing latency. Mitigation: conservative default mapping and offline kernel profiler to update hints.
Probabilistic admission might unfairly drop smaller customers under extreme burst; per-tenant credits mitigate but we need production telemetry to adjust defaults.
Attention-spike heuristic false positives could reserve fast-path capacity unnecessarily; tune threshold via A/B testing on production traces.
Complexity of decode handoff ticketing adds memory and race conditions; implement idempotent reservation with TTL and fallback to safe re-prefill path.
Feature flag misconfiguration during rollout could cause partial behavior leading to hard-to-diagnose tail spikes. Use canary and kill-switch with automatic rollback criteria.
comments: 2025-01-22 - Asha Patel: Initial spike completed. Benchmarked admission window heuristics on recorded production traces for 4 models. Observed 18-25% p99 improvements in synthetic mixed workloads with conservative settings.

2025-01-30 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype admission and probabilistic filter implemented. Added kernel_hint propagation from model registry. Need to add decode handoff ticketing; current prototype duplicates KV prefill occasionally.
2025-02-05 - Design feedback (Samira Cole): Console knobs look good; recommend exposing per-tenant credit visualization and an alerting rule template for customer SLOs.

2025-02-10 - QA (Jordan Li): Integration tests for microburst scenario failing intermittently due to race between reservation ticket expiry and decode arrival. Proposed TTL increase and idempotent rebind path.
2025-02-14 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented TTL and idempotent rebind; running full cluster soak on canary pool. Preparing rollout doc and kill-switch for runtime-1.19 release window.
